summary: The Castle’s translated map swaps its throne and adjacent floor. Lua row8 puts the throne at local x36 and floor at x37; JavaScript reverses them, so wizard mapping displays the throne one square too far right. RNG and cursors match; this is a bounded map transcription divergence.

source.branch: dat/castle.lua des.map long-string row8, local cells36/37; current JavaScript map literal in castle_levels.js40 swaps the backslash throne and period floor while preserving the63-column width.
callers: teleport.c:level_tele -> do.c:goto_level -> mklev.c:makelevel special-level loading selects dat/castle.lua. JavaScript mklev.js:ensureSpecialLevelLoaders1731–1767 imports CASTLE_LEVEL_LOADERS and selects its castle(des) owner; that owner passes its literal directly to des.map.

sp_lev.c:lspo_map6280–6292 traverses the map fragment and applies its terrain types. JavaScript mklev.js:mapFromRows4690–4736 maps each supplied character through splev_chr2typ and writes the canonical terrain; no caller or parser correction is required.

wizcmds.c:wiz_map -> detect.c:do_mapping1422–1444/show_map_spot1372–1419 -> display.c:magic_map_background233–258/back_to_glyph exposes the existing terrain after arrival. JS mapping/display reaches the same source path; it correctly renders the incorrect translated map data.
